chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a vineyard that has reached maturity, so he gives it to its cultivator (akkar) for such and such a number of 'danans' of juice, he said: 'No'.

key_terms.أَكَّارٍ: Cultivator (one who works the land for a share or fixed payment)
key_terms.دَنّاً: A unit of measurement for volume/quantity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying a vineyard cultivator with a specific quantity of juice?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarates the permissibility of *Muzabana* (selling a specific quantity of juice from a mature vineyard) when the produce is transferred to a cultivator (*Akkar*). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules 'No', indicating that this specific mode of contract is invalid, likely due to uncertainty (*Gharar*) in the exact yield or the nature of the exchange, distinguishing it from permissible sharecropping models.
